subject: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — onboarding gates and acceptance runway
messages:
From: Laura Jennings <laura.jennings@stellarhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com, alex.kline@stellarhealth.com

Subject: Re: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — initial ask

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. As discussed, procurement and legal need a clear sequencing plan so we can align internal approvers. High-level constraints from our side:
- Procurement needs a signed MSA + order form before any invoice is processed.
- Security needs the DPA finalized (privacy checklist passed) before data provisioning.
- Our legal team will run a single redline pass; exceptions escalate to our GC.

Can you send a short mutual action plan (MAP) that maps dependencies (MSA -> DPA -> order form), owner for each step, and recommended acceptance gates (pilot acceptance, SOC evidence review, SLA carve-outs)? We have a hard target: pilot launch week of July 19; procurement insists on a signature window of July 12.

Attachments: none

Laura Jennings
Sr. Procurement Manager
StellarHealth

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — initial ask

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. I sketched a proposed sequencing and owner model below; I can convert to a MAP spreadsheet and DocuSign packet once you confirm owners.

Proposed sequencing (short):
1) MSA commercial redline & order form draft (owner: Procurement/Buyer + Redwood AE) — target: sign by 2026-07-12
2) DPA / privacy appendix (owner: Legal teams, simultaneous review with MSA) — target: finalize by 2026-07-09 to allow data onboarding
3) SOC2 / security evidence handoff (owner: Redwood Security + StellarHealth security reviewer) — provide artifacts by 2026-07-05
4) Pilot acceptance criteria & runbook (owner: Customer success + Stellar ops) — acceptance window: 7/19–7/26

Quick asks:
- Who will be the final signature authority for the MSA at Stellar?
- Any specific DPA clauses you expect to revise (data residency, subprocessor list, breach SLA)?

I attached a lightweight MAP template and our SOC2 snapshot (Jan 2026). I'll loop in Vanessa from legal ops to call out any standard carve-outs we typically propose.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx; SOC2_report_Jan2026.pdf

Thanks — Rishi

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Jennings <laura.jennings@stellarhealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing MSA / DPA / Order Form — legal checklist

Thanks for the context — quick legal ops notes to surface so we can avoid rework: 
- We can run MSA redlines + DPA review in parallel but need a signed MSA (or countersigned order form referencing the MSA) before provisioning.
- Typical DPA negotiation points: data exportability, subprocessors, incident notification timing (we propose 72h), and deletion obligations.
- For SOC2 evidence we provide a summary package; if Stellar needs an on-site audit or NDA'd access to raw reports, that will add time.

Proposed legal gating rules: 
- Gate A (Security evidence): Redwood provides SOC2 summary + subprocessor list by 2026-07-05. If Stellar requests deeper artifacts, raise a scope item (may shift provisioning date).
- Gate B (DPA sign-off): Legal executes final DPA language no later than 2026-07-09. If there are material privacy changes, we recommend marking those as exceptions in the MAP and routing to GC.
- Gate C (Commercial sign-off): MSA + order form executed by 2026-07-12. Order form must list the pilot SKU and estimated seat/usage cap.

I'll prepare a redlines cheat sheet (what we typically accept, what we elevate). I suggest a single MAP sheet with owners, deadlines, and a column for "escalation required" so procurement can flag blocker items.

Vanessa Ortiz
Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi/Vanessa — two clarifications from procurement/legal: 
- Our final signatory for the MSA will be our VP of Product (Caroline Moss). Procurement can coordinate signature once legal confirms redlines.
- We cannot accept any wording that would require data residency outside the US. (Stellar is US-only).

Procurement is amenable to the proposed gates if Redwood can provide the SOC2 summary and a DPA draft by end of day Friday (2026-06-26). That would give our legal a week to review. If Redwood can hit that, procurement will push for the 7/12 sign window.

Also added procurement contact (procurement@stellarhealth.com) to the thread.
